title: Oleksandr Zinchenko ruled out for season after sustaining knee injury in second Ajax game
content:
Oleksandr Zinchenko has been ruled for the remainder of the season after sustaining a knee injury that requires surgery in just his second game for Ajax.

Just six minutes into the 4-1 Eredivisie win over Fortuna Sittard on Saturday, Zinchenko — making his home debut and first start — went down after battling for the ball with Dimitrios Limnios. The Ukraine international appeared to be in considerable pain and was treated on the pitch before being helped off the pitch by medical staff.

Zinchenko made his Ajax debut on February 8, coming on and played 14 minutes as a substitute in a 1-1 draw with AZ.

In a statement on Monday, Ajax confirmed the injury and that Zinchenko will be sidelined for “an extended period.”

“Examination at the hospital has shown that surgery is required,” the club said. “This will take place in the near future. The 29-year-old will then face a lengthy rehabilitation period, which means he will not play again this season.”

The injury could cast doubt over Zinchenko’s Ajax future, having only just joined the club from Arsenal on February 1 after cutting his loan spell at Nottingham Forest short. He signed a contract until June 30, 2026 but will now not appear for the side before the expiration of the deal.

He has also been ruled out of Ukraine’s World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final against Sweden on March 26 and appears unlikely to be available should his nation reach the tournament. The winner of the tie will play Poland or Albania on March 31, with the victorious team qualifying for the World Cup.

After making his debut for Russian side Ufa in 2015, Zinchenko moved to Manchester City the following year and spent six years with the club, winning the Premier League on four occasions. He joined Arsenal in 2022, where he spent three seasons and made 91 appearances.

Zinchenko signed for Forest on a season-long loan deal on deadline day in September, though he found game time limited and only featured 10 times before his loan spell was terminated earlier this month, allowing him to join Ajax.
